title: North America pilot · Four countries
edition: North America countries · Pilot · John · November 2026
intro: This is a North America pilot. First I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
We begin in the north with Canada and the United States, move down to Mexico, and finish on the small island of Jamaica.

states.name: Canada
lines: Canada occupies the northern half of the continent. From kanata, village in an Iroquoian language, Jacques Cartier took the name of the whole land in 1535.
It has the longest coastline of any country in the world, and Mount Logan in the Yukon is its highest peak at 5,959 metres.
states.transition: Let's bring the northern half of the continent into view.

states.name: United States
lines: The United States shares its northern border with Canada and its southern one with Mexico. America comes from Amerigo Vespucci, whose name a German mapmaker put on the New World in 1507.
Its largest city is New York, and Denali in Alaska is the highest point in the country.
states.transition: Now the country in the middle of the continent.

states.name: Mexico
lines: Mexico is the southern neighbour of the United States and the largest country in Central America. Its name comes from the Mexica, the people we call the Aztecs.
Maize was domesticated here, and the capital city still carries the name of the Mexica, Mexico City.
states.transition: Down into Mexico, from the border to the central highlands.

states.name: Jamaica
lines: Jamaica is a small island in the Caribbean. From the Taino Xaymaca, often read as land of wood and water, came its name.
Reggae was born here in the 1960s and Bob Marley took it around the world, and Blue Mountain coffee is grown in the mountains behind Kingston.
states.transition: Finally, a close view of a small island in the Caribbean.

recap: We covered four countries of North America: Canada in the north, the United States and Mexico across the middle and south, and Jamaica on an island in the Caribbean.

Canada is the second largest country in the world, the United States spans the continent, Mexico is the largest in Central America, and Jamaica shows how small a country can be and still have its own place.
